Apple released the first developer beta of iOS 27.2 six days ago, skipping the iOS 27.1 beta. A day after rolling out developer beta 2, Apple today released the first public beta of iOS 27.2, which includes an all-new iPhone Health app. Apple has also opened up the ability to schedule and purchase lab work through the new Health app via Quest Diagnostics.

iOS 27.2 beta brings all-new Health app, more

iOS 27.2 is the version following iOS 27, which launched on September 14. iOS 27.1 is only for iPhone Duo.

Apple has previously detailed how the iOS 27.1 SDK lets developers take full advantage of iPhone Duo's display capabilities. You can see here how apps look on iPhone Duo across different iOS versions.

Apple released Xcode 27.1 beta on Friday, adding an iPhone Duo simulator and app development support for the new foldable iPhone.

The first developer beta of iOS 27.2 includes the following changes:

  • The redesigned Health app, first announced by Apple at the iPhone 18 Pro event, makes its debut in this beta.
  • Group FaceTime gains a dual-camera sync recording mode.
  • Siri's AI language support expands to include French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.
  • Apple TV app profile functionality comes to iPhone.
  • Apple Podcasts' "Up Next" has been renamed "New Episodes". The "Continue Playing" section has moved below "New Episodes". Podcast episode lists also now feature a background that matches the topic color.
  • Apple Music has reduced its use of icon colors to label in-app tabs.

iOS 27.2 is expected to launch officially in October. iPhone users can currently get an early look at the new Apple Health app through the developer or public beta.
